question: What do the Cybersyn, OGAS, VSM and computerised planning literatures establish about cybernetic coordination?

item.title: Cybernetic Revolutionaries: Technology and Politics in Allende’s Chile

findings.finding: Cybersyn was to feature holistic system design, decentralized management, human-computer interaction, a national telex network, near real-time control of the industrial sector and modelling of dynamic systems; it was never completely implemented and ended with the 1973 coup.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: the system, known as Project Cybersyn, was never completely implemented

notFound: Quantities (telex machines, factories connected) are in the book body, not read.

item.title: How Not to Network a Nation: The Uneasy History of the Soviet Internet

findings.finding: Between 1959 and 1989 Soviet attempts to network the nation failed through unregulated competition among self-interested institutions and bureaucrats, whereas ARPANET (online 1969) succeeded through well-managed state subsidies and collaborative research environments.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: the Soviet network projects stumbled because of unregulated competition among self-interested institutions, bureaucrats, and others. The capitalists behaved like socialists while the socialists behaved like capitalists.

sources.population: Soviet attempts to build a national computer network, 1959 to 1989
notFound: Book body not read; figures are from the publisher description only.

item.title: InterNyet: why the Soviet Union did not build a nationwide computer network

findings.finding: Glushkov’s 1962-63 OGAS proposal (Statewide Automated Management System for Collection and Processing of Information for the Accounting, Planning, and Management of the National Economy) was slowed and emasculated by the Central Statistical Administration and Gosplan, each protecting its authority.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Instead of directly opposing Glushkov’s reform, central government agencies began to slow down and emasculate the project.

findings.finding: Without a network, 414 management information systems were built at enterprises and agencies in 1966 to 1970 with no coordination or connecting network.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: during 1966–1970, 414 such systems were built without any coordination or connecting network

findings.finding: Glushkov argued OGAS would control only information flows and warned that by the mid-1980s nearly the entire adult population would be engaged in planning, accounting and management unless processing was automated; his proposal to eliminate money did not gain Party support.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Glushkov’s proposal to eliminate money, however, never gained support from the Party authorities.

sources.population: Soviet national network proposals 1950s to 1970s: Kitov, Glushkov OGAS, Gosplan, Central Statistical Administration

item.title: Calculation, complexity and planning: the socialist calculation debate once again

findings.finding: Brute-force Gaussian elimination on a 10^7 by 10^7 system needs about 10^21 operations, about 1.5 million years on a mid-1980s supercomputer; iterative methods with 20 iterations give about 3 years; exploiting sparsity (100 direct inputs per product) with a linked-list structure gives about 10^3 seconds, 17 minutes.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: Under the same assumptions as above, but setting m = 100, we arrive at a running time of around 103 seconds, or 17 minutes.

findings.finding: The computation of the inverse Leontief matrix is within present-day capacity; the authors state the data-gathering problem is not addressed in this paper and endorse labour-time calculation supplemented by algorithms that let consumer choice guide allocation.
findings.exactSourceLanguage: We argue that labour-time calculation is defensible as a rational procedure, when supplemented by algorithms which allow consumer choice to guide the allocation of resources

sources.population: planning of an economy with about 10 million separately identifiable products
